## What was produced

`tests/org/apache/commons/lang/text/ExtendedMessageFormatAgentTest.java` — a self-contained JUnit 4 test class (matching `lib/junit-4.12`), package `org.apache.commons.lang.text`, class `ExtendedMessageFormatAgentTest`.

### How the spec drove the tests

The javadoc in `api/` documents only `ExtendedMessageFormat` itself (not `FormatFactory`), so every expectation rests on its stated contract:

| Contract in `api/` | Tests |
|---|---|
| *extends `java.text.MessageFormat`* | `instanceof MessageFormat`; format-element substitution, `{2}{1}{0}` reordering, escaped `''`, quoted `'{'`, `choice` sub-format thresholds, missing-argument placeholder, `getFormats()` order/types, `parse()`, `clone()`, `equals()` |
| 4 constructors, each *throws `IllegalArgumentException` in case of a bad pattern* | 4 dedicated `expected = IllegalArgumentException.class` tests (lone `{`, unterminated element) across all 4 constructor shapes |
| constructors take a `Locale` | `getLocale()` returns the passed locale; German vs US grouping proves the locale is actually applied; default-locale ctor honours the pinned JVM default |
| registry *consulted when format elements are parsed* / base formats *overridden* | empty registry ⇒ built-in `number,percent` still applied |
| `applyPattern` *applies the specified pattern* | re-apply changes both `toPattern()` and formatting output; malformed ⇒ `IllegalArgumentException` |
| `toPattern()` *overrides `MessageFormat.toPattern()`* | echoes plain text / simple patterns, stable across calls, and round-trips (rebuild-from-`toPattern` formats identically) including the escaped-apostrophe case |
| sub-format mutators *disabled, throw `UnsupportedOperationException`* | one `expected = UnsupportedOperationException.class` test each for `setFormat`, `setFormatByArgumentIndex`, `setFormats`, `setFormatsByArgumentIndex`, plus the unconditional (out-of-range index) case |

Default locale is pinned to `Locale.US` in `@Before`/restored in `@After` so locale-sensitive assertions are deterministic. No external helpers, no `git`, no bytecode inspection, tests not run.
